title: Authorization provenance workflow and evidence bundle
author: Elena Voss
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Authorization Provenance Workflow (APW) and the standard "evidence bundle" format used by Redwood Inference to capture, package, and retain authorization, RBAC, and audit artifacts for regulatory requests, post-incident forensics, and compliance audits. The APW complements existing audit-log pipelines and the evidence orchestration playbooks by focusing on reconstructing authorization decisions end-to-end (the provenance graph), packaging required artifacts, and providing a reproducible retrieval API.

Scope
- Applies to all production services that perform policy/authorization checks: authz-service, token-gateway, model-router, policy-evaluator, and platform-admin.
- Covers: authorization decision traces, entitlement bindings changes, session/session-key metadata, audit log tails, data-residency assertions, and cryptographic provenance signatures.
- Excludes application-level business logs (those remain in product-specific stores) but requires pointers/hashes to those logs in the bundle when used for forensic correlation.

Definitions
- Evidence bundle: a signed, timebound archive (JSON metadata + compressed artifacts) that contains everything needed to reconstruct an authorization decision and its context.
- Provenance graph: directed graph of actors (users, service principals), roles/entitlements, policy versions, and the evaluation path that led to a decision.
- Provenance snapshot ID: unique identifier (pb-YYYYMMDD-uuid) for a generated bundle.

Ownership and SLAs
- Primary owner: Security Control Team (security@redwood.ai).
- Supporting owners: Platform SRE (eng-infra), Product Security, Legal & Compliance for retention policy approval.
- SLA for evidence retrieval for live incidents: generate and surface a downloadable bundle link within 15 minutes of an authorized request (SLO: 90%). For accepted audit requests (non-emergency) maximum turnaround 72 hours.

High-level workflow (APW)
1) Triggering events
  a) Incident response runbook step (manual) to capture immediate evidence.
  b) Scheduled capture for high-risk changes (entitlement rollouts, emergency access).
  c) Automated capture when a cross-region data access event is detected (policy-evaluator alert).
2) Collection
  - authz-service exports decision traces to audit-edge with a provenance tag.
  - audit-edge streams relevant entries to evidence-collector.
  - evidence-collector queries: entitlement history, policy versions, user directory snapshot, session metadata, and the last N minutes of correlated app logs (via log-hash pointers).
3) Assembly
  - evidence-collector assembles the bundle JSON, attaches compressed artifacts (audit tail, policy diff, directory snapshot), and calculates a bundle manifest hash.
4) Signing & Storage
  - The bundle manifest is signed by KMS-backed service key (AWS-KMS or customer-provided HSM).
  - Bundle stored in evidence-store (region-aware bucket), with immutable retention attributes and a provenance snapshot ID.
5) Access & Delivery
  - Requestors (Security, Legal, SRE) use an authenticated internal API (GET /evidence/<pb-id>) to retrieve the bundle.
  - Delivery includes an access log entry and short-lived presigned URL when appropriate.

Evidence bundle format (required fields)
- bundle_id: string (pb-YYYYMMDD-uuid)
- created_at: ISO-8601
- producer_service: e.g., "evidence-collector@us-west-2"
- scope_tags: list of strings ["tenant:acme-corp","region:eu-central-1"]
- provenance_graph_hash: hex string (SHA256)
- artifact_manifest: list of {name, mime, size_bytes, sha256} (example included below)
- kms_key_id: string (key used to sign)
- signature: base64(signature)
- retention_policy_id: string (references retention catalog)
- access_control: role or policy name required to retrieve
- retrieval_log_id: pointer to the retrieval audit entry

Example minimal manifest (JSON snippet)
{
  "bundle_id": "pb-20260815-7b9a2f6e-1c4b-4c2f-9d2e-123456789abc",
  "created_at": "2026-08-15T18:23:41Z",
  "producer_service": "evidence-collector@us-west-2",
  "scope_tags": ["tenant:enterprise-x", "region:eu-west-1"],
  "provenance_graph_hash": "2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c",
  "artifact_manifest": [
    {"name": "audit-tail.ndjson.gz", "mime": "application/gzip", "size_bytes": "5242880", "sha256": "..."},
    {"name": "policy-diff.patch", "mime": "text/x-diff", "size_bytes": "1024", "sha256": "..."}
  ]
}

Evidence contents (recommended)
- Authorization decision trace(s) (ndjson): events emitted by authz-service with trace_id and parent pointers.
- Policy versions: the exact policy text (YAML/JSON) and the policy-evaluator binary or version tag used for evaluation.
- Entitlement history: audit records for role bindings and role-to-principal relationships, with before/after snapshots.
- Directory snapshot: user/service principal metadata, hashed PII redaction markers.
- Correlated application log pointers: either included log slices or hashes + retrieval instructions when logs are large.
- Data residency assertion: the runtime region and storage locations for any involved data (S3 bucket URIs, DB shard ids).
- Cryptographic signatures: KMS signature over the manifest and provenance graph.

Storage, retention, and lifecycle
- Evidence-store policy: bundles are stored in a region-mapped immutable store with bucket-level WORM enabled where supported.
- Default retention: 3 years for general bundles; 7 years for enterprise customers with contractual requirements or regulatory obligations (e.g., eDiscovery/regulatory). Retention is referenced by retention_policy_id and must be approved by Legal.
- Deletion/expunge: only performed via Legal-approved request and must include an expunge-log entry; deletion operations create an audit record in audit-edge.

RBAC integration and minimal access rules
- Retrieval of a bundle requires the "evidence_viewer" role or an explicit delegation ticket.
- Retrieval is logged to audit-edge with identity, timestamp, and purpose (free-text).
- Privileged roles (security-admin) have ephemeral elevation via JIT with enforced MFA for sensitive bundles.

Querying and reconstruction guidelines (for SRE/forensics)
1) Use the internal retrieval API: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://internal-api.redwood/evidence/pb-... | jq .manifest
2) Verify signature: evidence-cli verify --bundle /tmp/pb-... --kms-key arn:aws:kms:...
3) Rehydrate logs into the analysis sandbox using the provided log-hash pointers and manifest.

Incident playbook: when an authorization compromise is suspected
1) Run the incident triage checklist (see incident-response-security runbook).
2) Immediately trigger APW capture (manual: POST /internal/evidence/trigger with incident_id and scope).
3) Lock affected entitlements (policy-evaluator -> freeze-rule mode).
4) Generate a provenance snapshot and store it with retention-policy set to "forensic-hold".
5) Notify Legal and Customer Success if customer data or cross-border access is involved.

Validation, testing, and periodic audits
- Monthly smoke test: scheduled generation of sample bundles for canary tenants to ensure signing and retrieval work (owner: Platform SRE).
- Quarterly dry-run: full reconstruction exercise for a randomly selected authorization decision (owner: Security).
- Annual audit: retention policy compliance and key rotation traceability verified by Internal Audit and Legal.

Operational tooling and CLI examples
- Generate (service internal): POST /internal/evidence/trigger {"scope_tags":["region:us-west-2","service:model-router"],"ttl_minutes":60} -> returns pb-id and presigned download URL.
- Retrieve (auditors): evidence-cli fetch --id pb-... --out /tmp/pb-...
- Verify signature: evidence-cli verify --bundle /tmp/pb-... --kms-key-id alias/evidence-signer

Security controls and encryption
- All artifacts are encrypted at rest with AES-256; keys are managed in AWS-KMS by default. Customer-managed keys (CMKs) or HSM-backed keys are supported for Private deployments.
- Bundle manifests are signed; artifacts optionally signed (when required by contract).

Appendix: example provenance graph (text diagram)
User:alice -> [session: s-1234] -> authz-service(v=2.4.1) -> policy-eval(rule#42) -> decision: ALLOW -> model-router(route=dedicated-pool)

Appendix: minimal evidence bundle retrieval example (cli)
$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gimme-token)" https://internal-api.redwood/evidence/pb-20260815-7b9a2f6e-... -o pb-20260815-7b9a2f6e.tar.gz
$ evidence-cli verify --bundle pb-20260815-7b9a2f6e.tar.gz --kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01

References and related documentation
- See "event-schema-contract-and-retention-runbook" for audit log structure and retention hooks.
- See RBAC entitlement framework for role naming conventions and role-to-service mapping.
